subject: geography
title: Weather & Climate Adventure: Processes
welcome_lead: Why does the BBC weather map have wiggly lines? Today we decode depressions, anticyclones and fronts.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography Weather processes — depressions, anticyclones, fronts, synoptic charts.
final_note: You can now interpret a synoptic chart and explain pressure systems.

concepts.def: Low pressure system — wet, windy, unsettled
High pressure system — calm, dry, clear skies
Warm air rises over cold air — steady rain
Cold air pushes under warm — heavy short rain
Line joining points of equal air pressure
Unit of air pressure — average sea level ~1013mb

walkthroughs.body_html:
Low pressure (depression): air rises, cools, condenses — cloud and rain. Common over the UK.

High pressure (anticyclone): air sinks, warms, dries — clear skies. Hot in summer, cold/frosty in winter.

A depression has two fronts:

Warm front (semicircles): warm air gently rises over cold — light, steady rain over hours.

Cold front (triangles): cold air aggressively undercuts warm — short, heavy thunderstorms.

Isobars are lines of equal pressure measured in millibars.

Closely packed isobars = strong winds. Widely spaced = calm. A central 'L' = depression; 'H' = anticyclone.

options: Heavy rain and wind
Hot, dry, clear skies
Snow and ice
Thunderstorms

mcqs.q: On a synoptic chart, what do CLOSELY PACKED isobars indicate?
options: Strong winds
Calm weather
High temperatures
A warm front

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.
Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
Climate change only happens in summer.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Climate change only happens in summer.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
